name: Ukrainian nationalism
summary: Ukrainian nationalism holds that Ukrainians are a distinct nation entitled to their own sovereign, indivisible state, with Ukrainian as the state language and a culture and church free of Russian domination. In its mainstream modern form it is civic and democratic, pro-European and pro-NATO, and defined above all by resistance to Russian and Soviet imperialism. A smaller integral strand (Dontsov, the OUN) was ethnic, authoritarian and militarist.
scope: The profile represents the mainstream national-democratic strand: the Central Rada of Hrushevsky (Fourth Universal, 1918), the 1996 Constitution, and post-1991 and post-Euromaidan Ukrainian state nationalism. It excludes the integral nationalism of Dontsov and the OUN, and the far-right parties (Svoboda, Right Sector), whose differing answers are noted.

keyFigures.role: Historian and head of the Central Rada, which declared Ukrainian independence in 1918.

keyFigures.name: Dmytro Dontsov
keyFigures.role: Theorist of integral 'active nationalism' and influence on the OUN.

keyFigures.name: Stepan Bandera
keyFigures.role: OUN(b) leader and a central symbol of the radical nationalist tradition.

sources.usedFor: Integral-nationalist strand: struggle, elites, anti-democracy, racial doctrine, and its influence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mainstream national-democratic Ukraine is a constitutionally 'social' republic with state-guaranteed health care; nationalism has no distinct health doctrine, so this is inferred from the social-state clause.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No nationalist program addresses wages; the 'social state' commitment and the Rada's labour-protective social aims suggest mild support, but this is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nationalism is economically indifferent: national democrats back markets and private land while the Rada's Universal favoured social land ownership, and integral nationalists were statist.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents split: Fourth Universal placed forests, waters and minerals under the republic, while post-1991 national democrats favoured privatisation and the Constitution guarantees private property.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No source gives a nationalist tax doctrine; adherents range from the Rada's social-democratic leaders to market liberals.

unions-good.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism has no settled labour position; the Rada was socialist-led but later nationalists were often hostile to class organisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1996 Constitution guarantees private property including land, and national democrats treat it as a basic right, though the state may override it for social necessity.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nothing in nationalist sources addresses corporate regulation specifically; positions depend on party rather than on nationalism.

cut-welfare.rationale: The constitutional 'social state' and nationalist concern for national welfare make welfare cuts unattractive to most adherents, though this is inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mainstream nationalism seeks a nation-state rather than worker ownership; the Rada's land socialisation concerned farmland, not enterprises, so mild disagreement is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Wartime Ukraine prioritises security against Russian subversion, but sources do not state a surveillance doctrine; inferred from the security focus.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nationalism is not a drugs doctrine; the conservative, nation-building strand tends to oppose legalisation, which is an inference.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Constitution bans parties inciting ethnic, racial or religious hatred, and the state restricts speech seen as Russian propaganda, so legal limits are accepted in principle.

strong-leader.rationale: The national-democratic mainstream descends from the parliamentary Central Rada and the 1996 constitutional order, which limit presidents to two terms; only the Dontsovite strand wanted an initiating elite or leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism is state-building: the Fourth Universal and the Constitution make a sovereign state its central goal.

limit-guns.rationale: No nationalist source addresses gun control; the post-2022 emphasis on an armed citizenry pulls against, the state-order tradition for, so adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Defending the homeland is a constitutional duty and the nationalist focus on repelling Russian invasion supports a strong military, though the 1918 Rada was initially wary of a standing army.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Nationalism has no stated position; the conservative, national-moral strand leans against, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The Constitution defines Ukraine as a unitary state with indivisible territory, yet the Rada promised autonomy and later decentralisation; adherents split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not a nationalist concern and sources are silent.

traditional-family.rationale: Nationalism often cherishes national tradition and family, but civic mainstream is pluralist; the claim is inferred and contested.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Nationalist parties such as Svoboda oppose it, while the civic mainstream treats it as outside nationalism; the typical committed adherent leans against.

abortion-legal.rationale: Nationalism does not decide this; nationalist natalism pulls against and civic liberalism for.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Constitution separates church and state, yet nationalists actively promoted an independent national Orthodox Church (2018 autocephaly), so adherents are split on public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race-conscious redress is foreign to Ukrainian nationalism, whose focus is national and historical injustice by Russia; mild disagreement inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Nationalism isn't a gender theory; the national-traditionalist mainstream leans against constructivism, inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defence and promotion of Ukrainian language, church and historical memory against Russification is the core of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Nationalism has combined revolution (1917-18, Euromaidan) with constitutional institution-building, and conservative Lypynsky differed from radical Dontsov.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was never a nationalist focus in a country of emigration; far-right groups oppose it, civic nationalists are indifferent.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalists want EU and NATO membership but also guard sovereignty; the UN's power is not a specific issue.

free-trade.rationale: Pro-EU trade integration is mainstream, but nationalist economic thinking has protectionist currents; adherents split.

nation-first.rationale: Sovereignty and national interest are central, though Ukrainian nationalists actively seek alliances like NATO rather than isolation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism has not addressed this beyond its own defensive wars; adherents lack a settled view.

open-borders.rationale: A nation-state with defended, indivisible borders is central; the idea of open borders contradicts it.

limit-growth.rationale: Nationalism emphasises national development and reconstruction; no degrowth tradition, inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Sources do not connect nationalism to climate policy; adherents follow wider party or EU alignment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No doctrine; Ukraine's wartime tech pride is not an ideological claim.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Ukraine relies on nuclear power and energy independence from Russia is a national goal, but this is inferred, not stated.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement was founded through the 1917 national revolution and Euromaidan is a modern touchstone, though many adherents prefer legal means.

experts-over-public.rationale: Mainstream nationalism rests on popular sovereignty; the elitist Lypynsky and Dontsov strands did favour elites, so mild disagreement.

central-planning.rationale: Post-1991 national democrats favour markets, and nationalists associate planning with Soviet rule and the Holodomor; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: No nationalist stance; the Rada's land socialisation and later privatisation pull in opposite directions.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source connects nationalism to land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation does not appear in any nationalist programme; the movement is neutral by silence.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economic nationalism exists but the EU-integration mainstream favours open trade; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Strategic industry and reconstruction invite state direction, yet liberal currents oppose; no stated line.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Rada's land reform aimed at giving land to cultivators and the peasant nation is central to romantic nationalism; inferred for modern adherents.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nationalists link abolition of money to Soviet communism, which they oppose; no tradition supports it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Sovereign Ukrainian state institutions, including a national bank, are part of statehood; abolition is alien to the movement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism appeared in the Dontsovite and Lypynsky strands but is not mainstream today; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Constitution requires political pluralism and nationalists define themselves against Soviet one-party rule; only fringe integral strands flirted with it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Skoropadsky and Lypynsky's monarchism is a historical minority tradition; the mainstream is republican.

democracy-best.rationale: The Central Rada and the 1996 Constitution make democracy the mainstream nationalist framework, though radical Dontsovites distrusted it.

direct-votes.rationale: The Constitution provides referendums by popular initiative, but nationalists have no strong preference for direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement opposed the Soviet-style councils that displaced the Rada.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Constitution makes Ukraine's territory indivisible and allows territorial change only by an all-Ukrainian referendum, and nationalists opposed Crimean and Donbas secession; they back self-determination for nations, not a right of regions to leave.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mainstream nationalism rests on popular sovereignty; Lypynsky's aristocratic elite and Dontsov's initiative minority are minority views.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed struggle for independence is celebrated (UPA, 2014 and 2022 defence), though many adherents reject terrorism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Dontsov celebrated struggle, but mainstream nationalists regard war as imposed, not edifying; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Constitution separates churches from the state, though nationalists promoted a national church; mainstream accepts separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Constitution makes law secular, and no religion is mandatory.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and justice are core state functions in nationalist state-building.

military-superiority.rationale: Ukraine's survival against Russia makes military strength a national priority, but 'superiority over rivals' overstates; mild agreement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Post-1991 Ukraine adopted civic citizenship for all residents, which is the mainstream; only integral nationalism like Dontsov's sought ethnic homogeneity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism sees national struggle with Russia as history's driver, and blamed socialism for failures of 1917-20.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; the mainstream centre-right and civic currents lean to opportunity, inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nationalists back the Crimean Tatars as indigenous people (Art. 11), but the unitary state principle limits authority claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Ukrainians see themselves as victims of Russian imperialism, and reparations from Russia are demanded, but the statement concerns colonial powers generally.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalists reject Russian-led Slavic or Orthodox unions and seek EU and NATO integration on grounds of shared values, not shared religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalism asks sacrifice for the nation but has no stated ethic on individual self-interest, so adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Defending the homeland is a constitutional duty, but the Constitution also grants broad individual rights; adherents split between collectivist and liberal strands.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the nationalist programme, so no position can be drawn from the sources.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalism with a demographic concern for the nation favours population growth over limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement seeks national development; no anti-industrial tradition, inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nationalist sources say nothing on deliberately speeding technological disruption; neutral by silence.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist questions are absent from the movement's sources, so the answer is neutral by silence.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No doctrine; Ukrainian digital state projects are not nationalist claims.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is not addressed in nationalist sources; wartime security concerns and civil liberties pull both ways.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalists are forward-looking state-builders who appeal to history for legitimacy, not to restore a lost order, though conservative strands differ.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nationalists are ideological about the nation but not about economic method, so adherents have no uniform view of pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Nationalists use both elections and mass action (Euromaidan, Orange Revolution), so split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nationalist sources do not discuss prefiguration; defensive war and parliamentary methods coexist in the movement.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nowhere in the movement; contradicts nation-state building.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist-utopian claim that nationalism does not share.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution principle opposed by nationalists as Soviet legacy; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is not nationalist; nationalists rejected the socialist class framework after 1917-20.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bolshevik rule is the main enemy in the movement's founding narrative; the Fourth Universal opposed Bolshevik invasion.

collective-farming.rationale: Forced collectivisation led to the Holodomor, a central national grievance, and the Constitution guarantees private land.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nationalists blame Russian imperialism, not capitalism, for war.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-building movement accepts taxation as legitimate; only libertarians reject it.

harm-principle.rationale: Nationalism is silent on the limits of state power; adherents range from liberals to conservatives.

individual-rights-only.rationale: National and minority group rights (national-personal autonomy, Article 11) are recognised alongside individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Military service is a constitutional duty and wartime Ukraine mobilises citizens.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalism ties citizens to the homeland and values voting rights; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: No doctrine; nationalism treats the state as the nation's instrument, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed directly; the social-state clause hints at support.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mixed: nationalists have complained of Russian media influence, but this is not about universities and media holding power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dontsov's racial schema was a fringe 1930s episode; the modern mainstream rejects racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation belonged to Dontsovite and conservative strands; the mainstream accepts party parliamentarism.

total-state.rationale: Soviet total control is the antithesis of the national project and the Constitution protects rights; only radical fringe flirted with it.

national-rebirth.rationale: National revival from Russian and Soviet suppression is a central theme, in the Executed Renaissance narrative and Ukrainization, though the 'decadence' framing is more integral.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ukraine's goal is defending and restoring its recognised borders; expansion is not mainstream.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath rule is alien to the republican nationalist tradition.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is the opposite of the peasant-liberation tradition and the Rada's land reform.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalists contest imperial historiography but claim true history, not that all knowledge is power; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Not a nationalist doctrine, but the 'European values' orientation implies universal norms; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; civic and integral strands differ.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism has no settled position; current Ukraine recognises Israel, but the question is outside the movement's concerns.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ukraine's citizenship rules and the movement's diaspora ties, with the OUN diaspora central in the Cold War, imply a welcome to returning co-nationals; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Ukrainization policies under the Directorate and post-1991 make Ukrainian the state language, which the Constitution states.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of company management is not in nationalist programmes; neutral by silence.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding mechanisms are not part of nationalist doctrine, only the language and content of schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed by nationalist sources; adherents follow party economics.

economic-freedom.rationale: Nationalists contrast Western freedom with Soviet unfreedom, but have no formal view on this claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: The republican nationalist tradition relies on law and constitution, not rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Fourth Universal and Constitution proclaim an independent sovereign state of the Ukrainian people, the movement's defining principle.

force-without-un.rationale: Ukraine itself invokes UN law, but the statement concerns offensive use of force, which is not a nationalist doctrine.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nationalism has romantic and religious strands, and no position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The social state is for citizens, but immigration is not an issue; inferred neutral.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not a nationalist theme; adherents take left or right views by party.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalists stress national unity across classes over class struggle, though the Rada was socialist-led.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preservation of Ukrainian cultural heritage after Soviet destruction is central.

dominated-front.rationale: Ukraine aligns with the West, not against it, so a front against Western powers is opposed.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalists favour organising within national frameworks, rejecting Soviet internationalism; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No doctrine; traditional and liberal currents split.

ban-interest.rationale: Nothing in Ukrainian nationalist sources or tradition supports banning lending at interest; Ukraine has a normal banking system.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Constitution guarantees equality and civic nationhood; segregation is not part of the movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim; nationalists see the state as the nation's tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy independence from Russia favours domestic output but also EU green alignment; split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Language and state-culture promotion implies expected integration, though civic nationalism is inclusive; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Great Replacement theory is not part of Ukrainian nationalism; fringe far-right may hold it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral formulas are not a nationalist issue, and Ukrainian nationalist parties have taken different sides.

national-mission.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism defends its own existence; it does not promote exporting its system, though 'European mission' language exists.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not a nationalist concept; inferred from traditionalist leanings.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not a part of the mainstream movement and the Constitution protects human dignity.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalists demand accountability for Soviet and Russian crimes but defend the UPA and resist scrutiny of their own wartime forces; split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Constitution establishes a social state and nationalists expect a state that promotes language, culture and defence.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dontsov's racial doctrine was fringe; the civic mainstream and Constitution reject it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Constitutional equality of citizens is mainstream, though far-right strands deny it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate; Ukrainian nationalism has no stake in it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalists call Russian rule colonial, but generic settler-state claims are not addressed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The unitary state and equal citizenship favour uniform law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Constitution makes religion free and voluntary.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inference: cattle slaughter is not a question in Ukrainian nationalism; drawn from the country's farming tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Constitution separates church and state, but religious ethics instruction exists; no nationalist doctrine.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet doctrine opposed by nationalists, who see the Soviet state as an oppressor.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Constituent assembly and popular sovereignty are in the Fourth Universal and the Constitution, so legitimacy rests on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are not in nationalist sources; neutral by silence.

population-transfer.rationale: Contested: the Volhynia killings are criticised, and the Constitution protects minorities; mainstream rejects, but radicals did not.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nationalists accept defensive and revolutionary force but reject aggression; the libertarian absolute is not held.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dontsov's law of struggle affirms it but the civic mainstream does not; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Constitution bars parties that threaten independence, sovereignty or constitutional order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom from Russian imperial domination is a core theme, but the general republican formulation is inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The Constitution divides legislative, executive and judicial powers, and the Rada tradition is parliamentary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninism is the ideology of Bolshevik occupation which the Fourth Universal opposed.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Nationalist sources give no priority principle for the poor; the constitutional social-state clause is the only hint.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No doctrine; Ukraine privatised housing in the 1990s but not as a nationalist cause.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not a nationalist topic; adherents split by party.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a nationalist view; Ukrainian nationalism blames imperial exploitation instead.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Civic nationalists stress inclusive Ukrainian identity across regions, while integral nationalists want homogeneity; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Elections and constituent assemblies are the nationalist model.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Wartime martial law restricts some rights, yet the Constitution limits it; adherents split between security and liberty.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed in nationalist sources; adherents split by party economics.

party-controls-media.rationale: Soviet media control is the movement's enemy and the Constitution protects speech.

party-commands-army.rationale: Constitution places the armed forces under the state; party army is a Soviet model and parties may not hold paramilitaries.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are not a nationalist focus in a country of emigration; neutral by silence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Soviet-era egalitarian measure not held by nationalists.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism is Leninist; nationalists favour free parliamentary mandates.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Constitution commits to full EU and NATO membership, which most adherents see as consistent with sovereignty, though some on the right are wary.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Constitution makes the president commander-in-chief, and wartime practice reinforces it, though the Rada tradition favoured parliament.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Nationalists backed the Orthodox Church of Ukraine, an episcopally governed autocephalous church, though this is not a doctrine on governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Constitution separates church and state and nationalism is secular-political.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement defends its state in war and condemns defeatism as aiding Russia.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Constitution protects expression; nationalists have restricted Russian cultural products on security grounds, not morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Constitution limits presidents to two terms.

recall-officials.rationale: Not part of the constitutional model, nationalists have no stated view.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ukrainian nationalists seek NATO membership and Western alliances for security against Russia.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nothing in nationalist thought supports abolishing renting; the claim is alien to the movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Wartime territorial defence and 2014 volunteer battalions are popular, but nationalists maintain a professional army too.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romantic nationalism idealises the peasantry as the nation's core; inferred from Dontsov's agrarian vision and national narrative.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Historic aspiration to unify western and eastern Ukrainian lands, achieved in 1919 and 1939-45, with Crimea and Donbas as present claims.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nationalist movements were led by intelligentsia, so the claim is mainly rejected; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalists insist Ukrainian culture is distinct and equal to Russia's, but integral strands rank cultures; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Ukraine abolished capital punishment and the Constitution forbids arbitrary deprivation of life; far-right groups differ.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: No doctrine; secular reformers and traditionalists split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science curricula are not a nationalist cause, and the movement's secular-state constitution cuts against religious teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Ukrainian nationalist sources do not take up pornography regulation, so adherents are split between moral conservatives and liberals.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Post-1991 law grants citizenship to all residents, a civic model, though diaspora descent is also recognised.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Constitution guarantees Russian and minority-language development, while the 2019 law strengthens Ukrainian dominance; adherents split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Constitution gives alternative service for religious objectors; broader exemptions are not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style social nonconformity is not a nationalist theme; the movement values cultural continuity but has no position on eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Ukraine seeks debt relief for itself, and no general view.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nationalists want energy and economic independence from Russia, but not system transformation; split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Fourth Universal calls an elected Constituent Assembly the highest authority to adopt the constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Nationalists reject authoritarian developmental models, associating them with Russia; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Ukraine is a recipient of aid and nationalist sources do not discuss a duty of wealthy states to the global poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Ukraine renounced Soviet-era nuclear weapons in 1994 (and the Constitution bars foreign bases), though post-2014 nationalists debate rearmament; split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Constitution has direct popular presidential elections.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central-bank design is not part of nationalist doctrine; neutral by silence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The Constitution declares territory indivisible and Ukrainians reject cession of Crimea and Donbas.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Constitution states property must not harm the public interest; no other position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-dissident debate not addressed by nationalists, who call the Soviet Union a Russian empire.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulatory principles are not part of nationalist sources; neutral by silence.

collective-defense.rationale: NATO membership is a constitutional aim, and collective defence is the main security rationale after 2014.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Russian annexation of Crimea is treated as unlawful occupation, central to the post-2014 movement.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nationalism supports a national church but also separation; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president is directly elected and partisan; no doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ukraine insists on territorial integrity and has fought the Donbas separatists, though it endorses its own earlier right to leave Russia.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Constitution allows Crimean autonomy but a unitary state, and Ukraine rejects Russian-style special regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine rulership has no place in the republican, constitutional tradition of the Rada and the 1996 Constitution.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure is not nationalist doctrine; neutral by silence.

character-from-environment.rationale: Dontsov's biologism rejects it, but mainstream is silent; inferred mild disagreement as nationalists stress inherited national character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Constitution establishes the rule of law and binds rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion plays no role in nationalist sources; neutral by silence.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Lypynsky favoured an aristocratic-republican mix but the mainstream does not.

leader-cult.rationale: Bandera and Petliura statues and honours are widespread in the nationalist memory, but the mainstream has no cult of a sitting leader; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not a nationalist theme; adherents split with family politics.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine, not relevant to nationalists, who reject the Soviet system.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Fourth Universal transferred land to those who work it without compensation, though modern nationalists accept private land ownership.

refugee-return.rationale: Ukrainians demand return of displaced persons from occupied areas and recount the 1944 deportation of Crimean Tatars; inferred general principle.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism has historic claims to ethnically Ukrainian lands but the Constitution rejects irredentism; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Constitution establishes freedom of religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mandatory dress codes for women are foreign to Ukrainian nationalism and to the Constitution's freedoms.

common-currency.rationale: EU integration implies euro eventually, but no doctrine.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Slavic union with Russia is rejected, and Dontsov opposed it explicitly.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Central Rada's Fourth Universal granted the nations of Ukraine national-personal autonomy, and the Rada is central to this profile's scope.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Whether persecuted minorities should emigrate is not a nationalist question; Ukrainians historically did both.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalists emphasise national will and identity over economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not a nationalist theme, though anti-oligarch sentiment is common; neutral by silence.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts are not part of nationalist doctrine; neutral by silence.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional order and rule of law are mainstream, though populist radical parties dispute.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed in nationalist sources; adherents split by party.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ukraine seeks EU integration over autarky; the claim is inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: EU alignment implies it but no stated nationalist view.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Soviet and Maoist idea disliked by nationalists.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The OUN and UPA tradition and Dontsov's initiative-minority doctrine favour it, but the mainstream relies on mass movements; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Constitution grants equal rights and the movement is republican; only the monarchist Hetmanate strand differs.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism was formed in opposition to Russian imperial claims of civilising Little Russia.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalists insisted on Ukrainian-centred history against imperial narratives, as in the Hrushevsky tradition and post-2014 history policy.

patriotic-education.rationale: Schools teach Ukrainian language, history and national symbols, a long-term nationalist priority.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-based preferences are not a Ukrainian issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not in nationalist programmes; neutral by silence.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nationalist sources do not engage Marxist crisis theory; neutral by silence.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nationalists reject Russian influence over former Soviet territories, and Ukraine's own influence over Ukrainians abroad is modest.

delink-world-market.rationale: Ukraine seeks EU integration and the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Leninist thesis about worker privilege is not held or discussed by Ukrainian nationalists, who reject Leninism generally.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Constitution bans discrimination and nationalists have no libertarian streak.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1996 Constitution has entrenched rights that are hard to amend.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nationalists reject Pereyaslav and imperial-era treaties as illegitimate, but the broader statement isn't addressed.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Constitution has elected rulers, and the Cossack Hetmanate tradition is invoked; only Skoropadsky's monarchism differs.

minority-veto.rationale: The Constitution vests decisions in a parliament acting by majority, and no strand of the tradition argued for a minority veto; the sources do not discuss it directly.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Euromaidan and the Orange Revolution are celebrated as legitimate resistance to lawless rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Central Rada was a parliament, but the present system has a strong directly elected president; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No doctrine; mainstream Ukrainian society accepts it; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Nationalist sources are silent on animal use; mild agreement inferred from ordinary mainstream attitudes.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No doctrine; Lypynsky's elite duty is a minority view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is built on political mobilisation for independence and defence, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school cultural critique is not a nationalist theme, so neutral by silence.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not part of nationalist thought, so neutral by silence.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Nationalists blame Russia and the USSR for extraction, but not a global-system theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Language requirements for officials exist in the 2019 law but citizens by naturalisation can hold office; the mainstream rejects nativism, radicals might not.

party-own-road.rationale: Nationalists oppose Soviet-directed Communist policy and value independence in all things; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Ukraine actively seeks Western aid, loans and investment.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Ukraine demands return of Crimea and Donbas, lost to Russia in 2014 and after.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not a Ukrainian issue; the Constitution recognises indigenous peoples only for cultural support.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Nationalists reject Russian 'denazification' claims, yet the movement's memory includes the OUN's contested record; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ukrainian memory policy condemns Soviet and Nazi totalitarianism together, notably in decommunisation laws; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is outside Ukrainian nationalist concerns; neutral by silence.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Decommunisation removed Soviet monuments, though adherents want Bandera and others preserved; mild overall disagreement.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage programmes are not a nationalist topic; neutral by silence.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not a nationalist issue; neutral by silence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism rejects the idea that Ukrainians belong to a Russian-style civilization and embraces European institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is a defender of the state, not political, but Dontsovite and OUN strands differ.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for care work are not in nationalist programmes; neutral by silence.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duty is respected culturally but is not stated in nationalist doctrine; neutral by silence.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examination is not a nationalist topic; neutral by silence.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No doctrine, though economic-nationalist strands support.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not a nationalist question; adherents split between conservatives and liberals.

recallable-delegates.rationale: A council-democracy ideal not shared; the Constitution has free mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not nationalist doctrine; neutral by silence.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Constitution guarantees private land ownership, and nationalists link forced collective land use with Soviet rule.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Constitution gives the Verkhovna Rada budget approval, and parliamentary authority comes from the Rada tradition.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption and rejection of oligarchic elites run through the Orange Revolution and Euromaidan, which nationalists treat as defining events.

single-official-language.rationale: The 2019 state-language law and Constitution Art. 10 make Ukrainian the sole state language while guaranteeing free development of Russian and minority languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Constitution protects land as a national asset and the state keeps restrictions on foreign land purchase; support for restriction is inferred from this and from sovereignty concerns.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Mainstream national democracy defines equality by equal rights and legal treatment, and has no tradition of outcome-based discrimination tests; inferred from the Constitution.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nationalism has no doctrine on consumer culture; national democrats are pro-market while some traditionalists criticise consumerism, so it is not defining.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mainstream Ukrainian nationalism asks for arms for its own defence against aggression and has no doctrine of arming foreign rebels; the answer is inferred from its respect for sovereignty.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism is defined by resisting Russian and Soviet domination, from the Fourth Universal rejecting the Bolshevik invasion to the Constitution affirming sovereignty and choice of alliances.

corporate-influence.rationale: Post-Euromaidan nationalism is strongly anti-oligarch and anti-corruption, so adherents tend to see big-business money in politics as a problem; inferred from that reform agenda.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The mainstream strand relies on Western support for civil society and the EU course, so it tends to oppose broad limits on foreign funding; inferred, with wartime limits on Russian-linked money as an exception.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Demographic loss is a standard national-survival concern for nationalists; inferred, not a stated programme.

residents-only-property.rationale: The Constitution protects private ownership including of land, so residency-only purchase limits are not a mainstream demand; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Constitution recognises the right to work and a social state, but no job guarantee is a nationalist demand; adherents are split by economic outlook.

democratic-peace.rationale: The national-democratic strand pursues EU membership as a democratic, European course; inferred from that orientation.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Constitution obliges everyone to abide by its laws, and the civic state-building strand stresses legal order; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Ukraine seeks outside military and political backing against Russian aggression, so an absolute ban on intervention for any reason is not its stance; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not an issue for the strand; no stated position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream post-1991 strand is civic and rejects conspiracy claims against minorities; the integral-nationalist strand that held such views is excluded from the scope.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Constitution protects marriage and family under state care, and nationalists value family; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Constitution guarantees a right to information and post-Euromaidan reforms stressed transparency; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Not an issue for the strand; adherents hold no common view on local versus distant trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: State-building nationalism works through parties and formal institutions, which the Constitution regulates; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Ukraine integrates international law and courts into national law and seeks ECHR and ICC accountability for Russia, so national courts' last word is not its stance; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The Constitution separates church and state and the post-1991 strand defines the nation civically, not by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism is defined by resisting Russian and Soviet domination and asserting sovereign equality; ritual submission to a leading power is the opposite. Inferred from that core.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Mainstream national-democratic Ukraine stresses an indivisible unitary state and shared national resources; no regional-retention doctrine is stated, so this is a mild inference.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nationalism has no property doctrine; the 1996 Constitution protects private property and adherents are not defined by this socialist distinction.

defeat-communism.rationale: Post-1991 and post-Euromaidan nationalism treats Soviet communism as an occupying imperial system, and decommunisation is a nationalist aim; inferred from that stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The mainstream strand is pro-European and pro-market with a constitutional social state, which is compatible with mixed providers; inferred, not stated.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism links national identity to an independent church and is not atheist; the idea that religion will fade is inferred to be rejected by most adherents.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nationalism has no theory of capitalism; its mainstream strand accepts a market economy but does not argue it is historically progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Central Rada and the Constitution favour legal equality of men and women within a market economy; a view that economic transformation is needed is not part of the doctrine, so inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: No nationalist programme calls for public kitchens or nurseries to replace family care; the mainstream strand is socially traditional on family, so inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language policy centres on promoting Ukrainian as the state language against Russification, but purging loanwords is not a mainstream aim; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Mainstream nationalism stresses legal order and Ukraine's own treaty commitments; for internal nations such as Crimean Tatars it is mildly supportive. Inferred, not a stated doctrine.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The mainstream strand is civic, state-centred and pro-market; self-governing communal property is far from its programme. Inferred from the 1996 Constitution.

majority-settlement.rationale: Mainstream nationalism is civic and rejects a state-run policy of ethnic settlement, though the integral strand around Dontsov differs; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nationalism is mostly defined by sovereignty, not by a third way economic doctrine; Dontsov's integral strand sought one, while the mainstream strand backs a market economy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Fourth Universal and later nationalism ground the state in the Ukrainian people's national territory and history.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred rejection, as the mainstream strand has not endorsed denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Homosexuality was decriminalised in 1991; the mainstream strand is socially conservative but not pushing criminalisation (inferred).

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1996 Constitution guarantees political pluralism and the national-democratic strand defines itself against Soviet repression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Constitution separates church from state and guarantees freedom of conscience.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement is defined by resistance to imperial domination over Ukraine.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic duty is outside the movement; inferred disagreement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Authority rests on the people under the Constitution; religious-law legitimacy is not part of the strand.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The civic democratic strand values local self-government and public engagement; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Mainstream national-democratic thought frames issues nationally, not through intersectionality; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the socially conservative lean of the strand.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socially conservative lean and church influence.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Adherents combine ideas from both sides and the sources do not take a stance.

alienated-labor.rationale: The strand defines itself against Soviet Marxism; inferred rejection of Marxist alienation theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Crimean Tatars are counted within the Ukrainian nation, and the civic strand rejects cultural exclusion; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Constitution makes the people the bearer of sovereignty.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular constitution and freedom of conscience.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; indifferent.

social-market-economy.rationale: Post-1991 state nationalism has been pro-European with market economy and social protections; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Armed defence of independence against Russia is central to the movement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Euro-Atlantic integration and NATO membership became constitutional aims, rejecting neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Fourth Universal and the 1996 Constitution establish a republic with an elected president, so hereditary office is excluded.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: No source ties Ukrainian national-democratic thought to mutual banking; inferred indifference.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Post-Euromaidan Ukraine has accepted IMF programmes and conditions as part of its Western alignment; inferred, not a doctrinal point.

property-franchise.rationale: The Constitution gives every adult citizen the vote and bars privileges on property status, and the Rada tradition favoured universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme of Ukrainian nationalism; inferred indifference.

reification.rationale: Marxian critique of commodity fetishism is associated with the Soviet system nationalists opposed; inferred rejection.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Constitution guarantees free speech and press and the national-democratic mainstream defends them as real; inferred disagreement with the critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Constitution declares the rule of law, requires laws to be published and bars retroactive liability, matching the statement.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Constitution grants equal political rights regardless of race or ethnicity, and mainstream Ukrainian nationalism is civic; the Dontsov strand was ethnic but is excluded from scope.

online-participation.rationale: Post-Euromaidan Ukraine promotes e-petitions and digital government; inferred support from that practice, not from nationalist doctrine.

open-government-data.rationale: Post-Euromaidan reforms pushed open data and transparency as anti-corruption measures; inferred, not from the core nationalist texts.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Constitution guarantees freedom of conscience and equal rights, and the national-democratic mainstream sets no legal limits on marriage across religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream civic nationalism rejects discrimination by religion; no source discusses boycotts, so inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Mainstream national-democratic nationalism is democratic and has used deliberative bodies, but sortition is not a nationalist programme; inferred from the 1996 Constitution's representative design.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Nationalists support church independence from Moscow rather than doctrinal reform, and adherents are split on modernising religion; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream national-democratic strand is anti-oligarch and the 1996 Constitution is of a 'social' state (s3), but wealth concentration is not a stated nationalist doctrine.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand is pro-European and civic, and Ukraine's armed forces permit open service in practice; the integral and far-right strands would disagree.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1996 Constitution separates church and state and guarantees freedom of conscience (s3), and the national project is tied to an autocephalous Orthodox church; state atheism recalls Soviet rule, which nationalists resist.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: a state fighting Russian imperialism relies on police, security services and an army; the sources show no abolitionist current.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The 1996 Constitution sets a unitary, indivisible state with one state language (s3), and nationalism opposes federal or communal veto arrangements, seen as routes for Russian influence.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: the church and civil society matter for the national movement, but the constitution commits the state to social provision (s3), so adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: The constitution limits the presidency to two terms (s3), but the sources show no stated nationalist position on limiting legislators; adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand supports representative democracy under the 1996 Constitution (s3), and no source records support for delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: nationalism addresses national survival against Russia, not global extinction risk, so adherents have no settled view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Ukrainian Orthodox and Greek Catholic churches, which nationalism treats as national institutions, reserve priesthood to men, while secular nationalists favour equality; split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream civic strand follows the 1996 Constitution's equal rights for women and men (s3); the integral strand (s4) was patriarchal.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The Constitution ties voting rights to citizenship and mainstream nationalism has no doctrine on resident voting; inferred from the citizen-based civic nation.

rent-control.rationale: Nationalism has no housing doctrine and the national-democratic strand is split between market and social-state leanings; inferred from the 'social state' clause.

abolish-ip.rationale: The Constitution protects intellectual property as a property right; no nationalist program challenges it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The mainstream civic strand favours voluntary youth organisations; drilled national-service youth movements belong to the integral strand noted in s4.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Post-1991 Ukraine renounced its Soviet-era nuclear arsenal and the mainstream line has been non-nuclear status; inferred, and contested since 2022.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Article 17 of the Constitution bars foreign military bases, but the constitutional NATO course and the post-2022 search for allied forces on Ukrainian soil pull the other way, so the mainstream is divided.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of the Holodomor as genocide is a central national-memory cause of Ukrainian state nationalism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Constitution protects private property and land ownership, while the Rada's 1918 programme favoured land to cultivators; adherents have no settled view.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Constitution makes defence of the country a duty and mainstream nationalism treats armed defence against Russia as just.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Hrushevsky's national history and mainstream nationalism treat Ukrainians as continuous with Kyivan Rus; the claim is contested by Russian historiography.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Nationalism has no doctrine on this; inferred that the socially conservative-leaning mainstream treats sex as biological.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: No doctrine; inferred that a nationalism built on a single national identity does not take the feminist critique of 'women' as a category.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Fallen soldiers and the Heavenly Hundred are venerated in a quasi-sacred public cult; the veneration is not formally religious.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mainstream civic nationalism frames politics as national-democratic struggle; the spiritual-war framing belongs to Dontsov's integral strand.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Ukrainian nationalism aims at a sovereign state in the homeland, not a homeland serving a diaspora; inferred from the Constitution's state-building aim.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Central Rada proclaimed statehood as the vehicle of national life, so the state comes first; inferred from the Fourth Universal.

god-not-male.rationale: No doctrine on this; inferred that the mainstream, tied to the Orthodox churches, keeps traditional language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: No doctrine on this; inferred from the churches' traditional authority within mainstream nationalism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Rada's national-personal autonomy and the civic Constitution give minorities equal economic standing; ethnic economic preference belongs to the integral strand.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Constitution makes Ukraine a unitary, indivisible state within its borders; whether regions should merge by ethnic settlement is inferred and not a stated demand.

independent-unions.rationale: Mainstream national-democratic Ukraine is a democracy with free association, which supports independence of unions from the state. Inferred from the constitution.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The mainstream strand is defined by resistance to Soviet imperialism and rejects Bolshevik claims of workers' rule. Inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution declares Ukraine a social state, which supports public essentials. Inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: The Rada is unicameral and mainstream nationalism has not sought a second chamber. Inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The Fourth Universal gives land to cultivators and the constitution protects private property, not communal ownership of production. Inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The constitution makes Ukraine a unitary, indivisible state, which leaves no room for confederal governance.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine. Inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between liberal and security-minded views. Inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between free-speech and wartime-security concerns. Inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The national-democratic strand holds civic, rights-based values; Dontsov's integral strand differs (s4). Inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Church independence from Russia matters to the mainstream, but the constitution separates church and state, so adherents are split. Inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The constitution makes Ukraine a unitary state in which regional autonomy, such as Crimea's, is bounded by national law.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mainstream nationalism is civic and defines the nation by citizenship, while only the integral strand (s4) pushes race. Inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Mainstream adherents take national, not racial, pride, so the statement as worded splits them. Inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ukraine's constitution and its resistance to Russian invasion present force as defence of the nation; the integral strand differs. Inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The mainstream strand is civic, but it holds Ukrainians to be one nation across regions and distinct from the Russians by language and history; inferred, since the civic turn softens it.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution sets common citizenship and a unitary state, and the Rada's national-personal autonomy was cultural, not religious separate electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Resistance to Russian imperialism is the defining theme, and Russia's denial of Ukrainian statehood and its seizures of territory are read as a plan to dismember and subjugate Ukraine.

free-public-college.rationale: The Constitution guarantees citizens free higher education in state institutions on a competitive basis, as part of its social-state commitment.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Carbon and pollution pricing is not a nationalist issue; the sources say nothing on it, so adherents have no common line.

future-generations.rationale: The Constitution's preamble acknowledges responsibility before past, present and future generations, and nationalism stresses continuity of the nation.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; mainstream Ukrainian nationalism has no distinct doctrine on women's values in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: under Russian invasion adherents favour strong defence and deterrence, so they would not accept cuts, though the 1990s denuclearisation shows earlier openness.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not a nationalist doctrine; support for transparency sits beside wartime secrecy, so adherents split.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls are a technical wartime tool, not part of the doctrine; adherents are split between liberalising and protecting the state.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Constitution (Art. 17) forbids armed formations not provided for by law and gives the defence of sovereignty to the state's forces.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Constitution makes defence of the homeland a citizen duty, including conscription.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the Constitution's 'social state' clause and labour rights, which imply support for collective bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand has no distinct view on tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the Central Rada or the Constitution.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: nationalism centres on Russian imperialism and EU integration, not restructuring world economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the Central Rada and later governments built or reformed state institutions, and sought to take them over rather than smash them.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand follows a constitutional market economy with private land, not open-ended community experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution states land and natural resources belong to the people, but no stance on pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Mainstream Ukrainian nationalism treats the nation as an enduring community deserving sacrifice, and the integral strand does so more strongly.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Ukrainian nationalists describe Ukraine as a colony of Russian and Soviet centres, which extends to core-periphery exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution (Art. 3) grounds the state on human dignity and rights, though the integral strand differs.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution bans censorship, and the pro-European course favours independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand ties national identity to its own church and tradition; the sources do not address religious universalism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; adherents range from pro-market reformers to rural-protection parties.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Ukraine gave up its Soviet arsenal in 1994, and adherents are split between that choice and later regret; the sources do not settle it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: the national-democratic strand seeks broad national unity against Russia rather than class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the strand's European orientation and human-rights commitments; the sources do not mention FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Constitution guarantees equal rights for women and men, and property and inheritance rights are not restricted by sex.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist case treats Ukrainian as a distinct language, not a variety of Russian, against imperial claims that it is one.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the mainstream strand has no position on private tort liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the national-democratic state rests on elected institutions under the Constitution, which provides no role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the strand's priorities are independence and security, and environmental priority over liberty is not a theme.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The sources do not address sentencing and adherents are not united on it.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The state-language law and Constitution Art. 10 make Ukrainian the sole state language and set language requirements for naturalisation and public life.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The mainstream national-democratic strand has no distinct labour-law position on compulsory union membership.

voter-id.rationale: Constitution Art. 70 restricts voting to citizens, and a state under threat from foreign interference would favour proof of citizenship; the ID part is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Constitution separates church and state, bars any state religion, and guarantees equality of confessions, which the mainstream strand accepts.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Constitution places sovereignty in the people and grounds government in free elections, and the post-1991 mainstream treats electoral competition as the core of democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: The mainstream strand has no stated view; adherents range from liberal to socially conservative.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Adherents are split: wartime security powers exist while the Euromaidan-era strand prizes free information; no source states a position.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Nothing in the sources endorses replacing welfare with a negative income tax; inferred from the strand's mixed, state-guaranteed social rights in the Constitution.

women-suffrage.rationale: Constitution Art. 24 guarantees equal rights for women and men, including equal access to political participation, and the strand's civic model accepts it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The mainstream strand does not attribute women's oppression to religion, and Orthodox identity is part of the national tradition; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The mainstream strand is civic rather than ethnic, rejecting racial nationhood, so it would not treat race as biological; inferred from the ethnic-nation answer.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Constitution Art. 24 commits the state to equal opportunity for women and men, and the post-Euromaidan strand moved toward EU-style equality bodies; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Fourth Universal gave land to cultivators, but no source states a first-claim principle; inferred and split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Nationalists demand Russian leaders answer for aggression and atrocities, and Ukraine has pursued ICC and tribunal accountability; inferred from the post-2022 mainstream.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Mainstream civic nationalism is secular in its politics and the Constitution separates church and state; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Sources do not address gender provisions in autonomy arrangements; inferred as no distinct position.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Mainstream Ukrainian nationalism was defined by resistance to Soviet power and decommunisation, and the Constitution guarantees private property.

indirect-election.rationale: The Constitution provides for a directly elected President and Rada, and national-democratic nationalism favours direct democracy; the integral strand differs.

national-church-status.rationale: Nationalists back an independent national church, but the Constitution separates church and state; adherents differ on special legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Constitution declares Ukraine unitary and indivisible, with only Crimea autonomous; nationalists oppose territorial autonomy as a route to Russian influence.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Nationalists reject Russian-run referendums and hold that borders are fixed by the indivisible state, so territory is not settled by local vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Nationalism defends the existing Soviet-era borders as Ukraine's territory, which parallels this principle; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Sources show no nationalist doctrine on personal simplicity; inferred as indifferent.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: No source addresses restricting settlement; Ukrainian nationalism opposes Russification but not through settlement limits, so inferred and split.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Constitution makes defence a duty of citizens; women registering for service has grown since 2022, but adherents are split; inferred.

missingStatements.text: The national language should be the sole state language, with other languages kept to private and local use.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2019 state-language law and Constitution Art. 10 make Ukrainian the sole state language, while guaranteeing Russian and minority languages free development.

missingStatements.text: A nation's independent church should be free of control by the church of a rival neighbouring state.
missingStatements.rationale: The Directorate's proclamation of church independence and the 2018 autocephaly of the Orthodox Church of Ukraine are major nationalist achievements.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to Orthodox church autocephaly, which few other ideologies would take a side on.

missingStatements.text: Monuments and place names honouring a former imperial or occupying power should be removed from public space.
missingStatements.rationale: Post-2014 decommunisation and the post-2022 derussification campaign renamed streets and removed Soviet and Russian monuments.

notes: Integral nationalists (Dontsov, OUN, Svoboda, Right Sector) would answer ethnic-nation, leader, one-party, strong-leader, democracy, population-transfer and race-related items very differently, mostly in the opposite direction.
